title: Find the first NaN in a bounded double array
summary: Two different quiet NaN encodings select the first NaN at or after the clamped start. Both zero signs have the same search index.

change.description: Two different quiet NaN encodings select the first NaN at or after the clamped start. Both zero signs have the same search index.

notes: Each bounded array word is paired with every start from -1 to length+1. The final selector is the five-element infinity and NaN regression.
The captured original module and its dependencies are identified by SHA-256. The setup record retains build and historical regression evidence.

The parent returned −1 for the named NaN search and the fix returned index 1. The fixed first-match and both revisions’ signed-zero and finite controls were established on the opening native verifier. The grid uses exact quiet-NaN bit patterns and tolerance zero.

At tolerance 0.25 and centers −0.5, 0 and 0.5, strict native proofs on both historical revisions cover two independent binary64 cells and every Java int start. The caller quiets signaling NaNs before constructing the array. Both JVMs agreed with the exact-rational oracle on 18,900 cases each. Excluding either endpoint changed 564 results, and selecting the last match changed 582.
